issues.failure_explanation: The singular values of the Kronecker sum L = I⊗A + A⊗I are not twice those of A. L has eigenvalues λ_i+λ_j. Take A normal with eigenvalues -ε±iω. Then L has eigenvalue -2ε, so σ_min(L) ≤ 2ε, whereas 2σ_min(A) = 2√(ε²+ω²). The claimed equality therefore fails, and the bound ||E|| ≤ ||R||_F/(2σ_min(A)) can underestimate the error by an arbitrary factor. The same false value of ||L^{-1}|| is reused in the bound eq33 and in the scaling eq:52 meant to ensure γ ≤ 1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 2σ_min(A) by σ_min(L) (the separation), or by a valid computable lower bound such as -2λ_max((A+A^T)/2) when A is dissipative. Then redo eq33, the scaling and the tolerance splitting with the new constant.
issues.overall_effect: The residual-based certificate, the computable bound on ||L^{-1}Π||, the rescaling rule and the main guarantee ||X - X̃|| ≤ tol of teo1 are all unreliable for non-symmetric A_j.
issues.title: False identity sigma_min(L) = 2 sigma_min(A) underlying the certified Lyapunov error bound
issues.why_classification: The certified O(n) error guarantee is the main contribution. A valid computable lower bound on σ_min(L) exists only under extra assumptions such as dissipativity, so the advertised generality or cheapness is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: Dissipativity only gives w^T A_j^T w ≤ λ_max((A_j+A_j^T)/2)||w||^2. In general -λ_max(sym A_j) ≤ σ_n(A_j), often strictly. Example: normal A with eigenvalues -ε±iω has w^T A w = -ε||w||^2 but σ_n = √(ε²+ω²). The used inequality points the wrong way, so μ ≥ κ(A_j)||X - X̃|| does not ensure the LMI.

issues.failure_explanation: The GLE solutions with A = A_j are not the standard Gramians of mode j. They satisfy only non-strict Lyapunov inequalities. Truncating a balanced realization under such inequalities gives Â_jΣ_1 + Σ_1Â_j^T + B̂_jB̂_j^T ⪯ 0, which yields only Re λ ≤ 0 (marginal stability). The classical asymptotic-stability result for square-root balanced truncation assumes exact Gramians and is invoked without checking its hypotheses.
